audit_findings.title: Equity-method stakes may be double counted
audit_findings.magnitude: up to CAD 19,410 million, equal to 47.0% of base equity value or CAD 8.80 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings enter the OE numerator through common earnings, while the stakes_net amount is added again in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Equity investments over which we exercise significant influence, but do not have controlling financial interests, are accounted for using the equity method.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that equity-method earnings are included in consolidated earnings and that CAD 19,410 million of stakes is added to the valuation bridge. Whether the OE calculation removed every corresponding investee earning remains unresolved. Because the bridge addition supplies nearly half of base equity value, unreconciled overlap is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile stakes_net asset by asset to the CAD 2,224 million of 2025 income from equity investments and the OE calculation; remove either each stake's earnings from OE or its separately added value, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain material non-operating gains
audit_findings.magnitude: CAD 1,500 million net positive 2025 impact, equal to 100.3% of the CAD 1,495.4 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrealized derivatives, investee disposition gains and impairments enter common earnings and therefore the OE anchor unless explicitly normalized.
audit_findings.evidence: Earnings attributable to common shareholders was positively impacted by $1.5 billion due to certain infrequent or other non-operating factors, primarily explained by the following:
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a net CAD 1.5 billion positive effect from infrequent or non-operating factors, including a CAD 999 million after-tax unrealized derivative gain and a CAD 65 million after-tax DCP disposition gain, partly offset by impairments. The supplied record does not demonstrate their removal from OE. Retaining the net positive amount could dominate the anchor and materially overstate every scenario, although individual impairment adjustments must be treated consistently.
audit_findings.action: Produce the line-by-line reconciliation from CAD 7,072 million of reported common earnings to CAD 1,495.4 million of OE, distinguish realized hedge settlements from unrealized marks, normalize identified gains and impairments consistently, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter may ignore a post-deadline Line 5 shutdown obligation
audit_findings.magnitude: US$1,000 million sanctioned relocation project; shutdown, remediation and lost-throughput effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A shutdown or operating restriction would reduce forecast OE and growth, while relocation and remediation would alter capital needs and the operating perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 27, 2026, Enbridge filed a Motion to Stay or Modify the portion of the Court’s June 29, 2023 Final Judgment requiring Enbridge to cease operation of Line 5 on any parcel without a valid right-of-way by June 16, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: A current shutdown is not demonstrated: the latest filing says the June 16, 2026 shutdown order was stayed, and the July 30, 2026 appellate decision dismissed the nuisance claim, affirmed trespass and remanded remedies. Enbridge also sanctioned a US$1.0 billion relocation targeted for early 2027, with recoverable capital expected to enter Mainline rate base. The continuing trespass and remand nevertheless create forward-looking shutdown, timing and remediation risk not represented by a null perimeter.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the district-court remedy and Line 5 operating status as of September 4, 2026; monitor relocation timing and rate recovery, and rerun the perimeter if an enforceable restriction, unrecoverable expenditure or throughput loss emerges.

audit_findings.title: Regulatory deferrals can hide current cash operating costs from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: CAD 1,290 million of identified deferred-project and demand-side-management regulatory assets, equal to 86.3% of anchor OE; annual net cash deferral unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash operating expenditures capitalized into regulatory assets can bypass both current earnings expense and PPE capex deductions, while later rate recovery and amortization affect future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: With the approval of regulators, certain operations capitalize a portion of specified operating costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate CAD 1,105 million of deferred-project regulatory assets and CAD 185 million of demand-side-management assets. Those are balance-sheet stocks, not the annual omitted cash amount, so they do not establish the valuation error. Current OE could be overstated by unrecognized cash deferrals, while omitted future recoveries could offset or reverse part of the effect; the timing and present-value impact remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 additions, cash payments, recoveries and amortization for each relevant regulatory asset, identify amounts excluded from PPE capex, incorporate both the cash deferral and later recovery, and rerun if the net timing effect changes anchor OE.

audit_findings.title: Woodfibre guarantees create an unrecognized claim on parent cash
audit_findings.magnitude: CAD 2,400 million estimated maximum guarantee exposure, equal to 5.8% of base equity value or CAD 1.09 per diluted share; expected loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected guarantee payments or committed funding reduce the common-equity bridge and may also reduce future OE; adding the investment without those claims can overstate value.
audit_findings.evidence: Although some guarantees do not contain contractual limitations on potential future payments, our undiscounted estimated maximum exposure to loss related to these guarantees as at December 31, 2025 is approximately $ 2.4 billion (2024 - $ 1.9 billion).
audit_findings.explanation: The CAD 2.4 billion maximum exposure is filed and large relative to the CAD 1.495 billion anchor, but it is an undiscounted maximum rather than an expected loss. The record also notes indemnification rights and does not establish the probability, timing or net amount of a payment. The valuation effect may be meaningful, but materiality cannot be established from maximum exposure alone.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the guarantee schedule, default probabilities, expected payment timing, remaining funding commitments and enforceable indemnification recoveries; calculate a probability-weighted net claim and deduct it from stakes_net or forecast OE before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI requires claim-consistent terminal treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: CAD 736 million current redeemable NCI, equal to 1.8% of base equity value or CAD 0.33 per diluted share; 2035 fair-value redemption amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Common OE must exclude the 12.47% minority cash flows while the interest remains outstanding; any future redemption payment must be paired with the incremental cash flows acquired thereafter.
audit_findings.evidence: Westcoast Energy Limited Partnership’s (Westcoast LP) Class A noncontrolling unitholder has the option, exercisable at any time from and after July 2, 2035, to require the Class B and Class C unitholders of Westcoast LP to redeem all of the Class A units for cash at the then-current fair value, subject to certain limitations.
audit_findings.explanation: The current CAD 736 million claim alone is modest relative to CAD 41,301 million of base equity value, and common earnings already deduct NCI earnings. However, redemption is at then-current fair value from 2035, so the ultimate payment may differ materially from the current carrying amount. The record does not show whether terminal OE continues to exclude the minority share or assumes ownership after redemption, leaving the net direction and materiality unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 12.47% minority allocation through forecast and terminal OE; model either continuing minority ownership or a 2035 fair-value redemption together with the acquired minority cash flows, then compare both treatments.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: CAD 95 million in 2019, 2.8% of filed 2019 D&A; CAD 0 effect on the current anchor under the stated MIN(trend, latest) rule
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would increase historical OE if added back and could affect the trend calculation, but it does not change the latest-year OE used as the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $95.0m (2.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The uncertainty is demonstrably conservative: any eligible reclassification could only raise 2019 OE. The CAD 2,930 million trend already exceeds the CAD 1,495.4 million latest-year anchor by CAD 1,434.6 million, so adding at most CAD 95 million to 2019 cannot change the MIN(trend, latest) anchor or the current valuation scenarios.
audit_findings.action: No valuation rerun is needed unless filed evidence identifies eligible residual D&A in 2025 or a broader correction changes the anchor-selection rule; otherwise retain the conservative expense treatment.
